content.text:
Yes, it's possible — and that's what's now implemented. You can add as many OpenAI-compatible endpoints as you want, each identified as `openaiCompatible/<name>`, alongside the built-in providers.

**How it works**

A provider ID is either a built-in kind (`openai`, `anthropic`, `qwen`, …) or a named instance of the compatible kind, e.g. `openaiCompatible/my-vllm`. The shared type is now `LlmProviderKind | \`openaiCompatible/${string}\``, and small helpers (`providerKind`, `providerName`, `providerLabel`, `toProviderName`) resolve the kind for metadata lookups and the name for display. Everything that used to index `PROVIDER_META[provider]` now goes through `providerKind(provider)`, so named instances inherit the compatible kind's capabilities without duplicating config. The database needed no migration: `project_llm_config.provider` is text with a unique `(project_id, provider)` constraint, which already allows several named rows.

**Where you can declare them**

In the settings UI, picking "OpenAI-compatible" reveals a required Name field with live normalization (`My vLLM` becomes `my-vllm`) and validation, plus the base URL and optional API key. In `nao_config.yaml` you write `provider: openai-compatible/my-vllm` and the CLI normalizes and validates it, rejecting names on non-compatible kinds and duplicate IDs while allowing multiple compatible instances. The interactive `nao init` prompt asks for a name and lets you add more than one.

One deliberate limitation: `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL` configure only the single unnamed endpoint. Named instances don't silently inherit them, since that would make several endpoints share one key and URL; the CLI skips named instances when building the LLM env. This is noted in `.env.example` and in the docs, where I added an "Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint" section to both the configuration reference and the admin setup page.

**Verification**: `npm run lint` passes with zero errors (three warnings remain in `chart.tsx` and the usage route, all pre-existing and unrelated), `cd cli && make lint` is clean, the 74 backend inference-option tests pass including new ones covering options keyed under the full instance name and error messages that name the instance, the 4 new shared helper tests pass, and the 30 CLI config tests pass. The shared workspace's own vitest install is broken by a `tinyrainbow` export mismatch that predates this work, so I ran that file with the backend's vitest binary.

content.text:
Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints now show their own site favicon, greyed out, instead of the generic server glyph — and the MCP favicon logic that inspired it got fixed along the way.

What changed:

- `apps/frontend/src/lib/favicon.ts` replaces `mcp-favicon.ts`. Same same-origin-only policy (no third-party favicon API, as the old test insisted), but it now also falls back to the parent domain when the host has three or more labels. That's the fix for "not sure it works well": an endpoint like `https://api.acme.com/v1` almost never serves `/favicon.ico` itself, while `acme.com` does.
- `apps/frontend/src/components/ui/favicon.tsx` is a small shared component that walks the candidate list, dropping each one that fails to load, and renders a fallback node when nothing loads. `McpServerIcon` and `LlmProviderIcon` both use it, so MCP servers and LLM endpoints behave identically.
- `LlmProviderIcon` takes an optional `baseUrl`. Only the `openaiCompatible` kind uses it (every other provider has a brand SVG); the image gets `grayscale` on top of the existing `opacity-50`, and the `Server` icon remains the fallback for endpoints without a favicon, which is what you'll see for a local vLLM.

To make the icon useful outside the settings page, `getProjectAvailableModels` now returns each model's `baseUrl` (from the DB config, then `nao_config.yaml`, then the env var). That flows into the chat model picker, the automation model select, the recommendations settings, and the Slack/Teams/Telegram/WhatsApp sections, so several named endpoints are distinguishable wherever models are listed. Non-admins already received base URLs through `getLlmConfigs`, so this exposes nothing new.

One caveat worth knowing: the favicon is fetched by the user's browser, so an endpoint only reachable from the server (an internal vLLM, say) will always fall back to the server glyph. That's deliberate — proxying icons through the backend would mean it makes outbound requests to arbitrary admin-supplied URLs.

The issue is that `localStorage` isn't available in the default Node test environment, and while jsdom could provide it, the repo has ESM compatibility issues with jsdom. I'll stub `globalThis.localStorage` directly in the test with a simple in-memory implementation instead.

I need to handle the module-level `lookups` variable that persists across tests by resetting modules between test cases and dynamically importing the favicon module fresh each time. I'm writing a helper function to stub localStorage and then creating tests that verify the caching behavior: checking that `resolveFaviconCandidates` returns all guesses initially, that `rememberFavicon` caches a specific source, that passing `null` clears the cache, that verdicts are shared across paths on the same origin, and that cached verdicts survive a page reload by reading from localStorage after a fresh module import.

The issue is that `vi.resetModules()` in beforeEach doesn't actually reset the static `./favicon` import, so the module's `lookups` state persists across tests in the same file. This makes test order fragile—a test like 'tries every guess for a service it knows nothing about' could fail if a previous test cached acme.com. The `getFaviconCandidates` describe block doesn't have this problem since it doesn't retain state, but the current approach is still brittle and needs a better solution.

The cleanest fix is to use dynamic imports in each test after calling `vi.resetModules()`, so each test gets a fresh module instance. For the caching describe block, I'll restructure it to import the favicon module dynamically inside each test rather than relying on the static import. The pure `getFaviconCandidates` tests can keep using the static import since they don't depend on state. For the "keeps what it found across page loads" test, I'll use one instance to remember a value, then load fresh and verify it persists. I also need to be careful with the `stored` map and `vi.stubGlobal`—that's what creates the persistence across "page loads" simulation, which is correct. There's a potential issue with fake timers and dynamic imports that I need to watch out for.
